'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[2022–2023 Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure]], [[Moldova–Russia relations]]
***[[Moldova]] says that [[Russia]] has fired [[missile]]s over the country at targets inside [[Ukraine]], condemning the missile flyover as a violation of its sovereignty, and also summons the [[List of diplomatic missions of Russia|Russian ambassador]] for an official explanation. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-64593488 (BBC News)]
**[[Southern Ukraine campaign]]
***A [[Russian Navy]] [[unmanned surface vehicle|drone boat]] strikes the [[Zatoka, Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi Raion, Odesa Oblast|Zatoka]] railway bridge on [[Highway H33 (Ukraine)|Highway H33]] near [[Odesa]]. It is believed to be the first use of the naval weapon in the war by Russian forces. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2023/02/11/ukraine-invasion-russia-strikes-key-odessa-bridge-drone-boat/ (''The Telegraph'')]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[2023 Ramot Junction attack]]
***Three [[Israel]]is, two brothers aged six and eight years old and a 20-year-old man, are killed in a [[car-ramming attack]] in [[Ramot, Jerusalem]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/at-least-6-wounded-2-seriously-in-suspected-car-ramming-attack-in-jerusalem/ (''Times of Israel'')]
*[[Balochistan conflict]]
**Two people are killed and three others are injured when a vehicle hits a [[roadside bomb]] in [[Kohlu District]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/afghanistan-iran-politics-violence-85d906ca1d4c766811d6075246b15e8d (AP)]
*[[Islamist insurgency in the Sahel]]
**At least ten [[Niger Armed Forces|soldiers]] are killed and thirteen others are injured in an [[ambush]] by [[jihadists]] in [[Tillabéri Region]], [[Niger]]. Sixteen others remain missing. [https://punchng.com/terrorists-kill-10-niger-soldiers/ (AFP via ''The Punch'')]
*[[List of high-altitude object events in 2023|High-altitude object events in 2023]]
**[[2023 Alaska high-altitude object]]
***The White House's spokesperson [[John Kirby (admiral)|John Kirby]] announces that the [[United States Air Force]] shot down a high-altitude object over territorial waters in [[Alaska]], just days after shooting down a [[2023 Chinese balloon incident|Chinese balloon]] over the [[Atlantic Ocean]]. The object was ordered to be shot down by [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] because it posed "a reasonable threat to the safety of civilian flight". [https://thehill.com/policy/defense/3852988-us-shoots-down-another-high-altitude-object-over-alaskan-airspace/ (The Hill)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Great Yarmouth explosion]]
**A [[World War II]]-era bomb weighing around 250kg explodes while being [[Bomb disposal|defused]] in [[Great Yarmouth]], [[Norfolk]], [[England]]. No injuries are reported. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-norfolk-64604115 (BBC News)]
*Two people are killed and 20 others are injured in a [[building collapse]] in [[Damanhour]], [[Beheira Governorate]], [[Egypt]]. [https://apnews.com/article/egypt-business-building-collapses-8b6ab7158b0fe480901ff67516e6ccdd (AP)]
*At least 35 people are injured when a bus overturns near [[Magdeburg]], [[Saxony-Anhalt]], [[Germany]]. [https://apnews.com/article/automotive-accidents-berlin-belgium-poland-7678e8cbf5d69aec177dd6c6170eb635 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2017–present Peruvian political crisis]]
**[[2022–2023 Peruvian protests]]
***The [[Parliament of Peru#The Permanent Assembly|Permanent Assembly of the Congress of Peru]] approves a motion to file criminal charges against former president [[Pedro Castillo]]. The charges include criminal organization, traffic of influences, and collusion. [https://www.lanacion.com.ar/agencias/la-comision-permanente-del-parlamento-de-peru-aprueba-acusar-al-expresidente-castillo-de-nid10022023/ (europapress via ''La Nación'')]
*[[Crime in South Africa]]
**Two people, including [[South Africa]]n rapper [[AKA (rapper)|AKA]], are shot dead outside a restaurant in [[Durban]], [[KwaZulu-Natal]]. The assailants fled the scene on foot, according to police. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-64608537 (BBC News)]
*A [[Judiciary of Hong Kong|Hong Kong court]] awards an [[Indonesian migrant worker|Indonesian]] [[Foreign domestic helpers in Hong Kong|domestic worker]] more than {{HKD|860,000|link=yes}} ({{USD|110,000|link=yes}}) in [[damages]] for the [[Maid abuse|abuse]] she received from her former employers, who were [[Conviction|convicted]] and [[Imprisonment|imprisoned]] in 2013. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/indonesian-maid-wins-145000-in-compensation-for-abuse-in-hong-kong (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Prime Minister of Moldova|Moldovan prime minister]] [[Natalia Gavrilița]] [[resign]]s amid an economic crisis and the collateral effects of the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|ongoing war in neighboring Ukraine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/moldovan-prime-minister-announces-government-resignation-2023-02-10/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mayor of Toronto|Toronto mayor]] [[John Tory]] announces he will be resigning following revelations he had an extramarital affair with a staffer during the COVID-19 pandemic. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/toronto-mayor-john-tory-statement-1.6745144 (CBC)]

***[[Hatayspor]] withdraws from the [[Süper Lig|top division]] of Turkish football due to the earthquake. [https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/hatayspor-withdraw-turkish-league-after-earthquake-clubs-union-president-2023-02-09/ (Reuters)]
